Work top to bottom. Check the box when done, note what you found.

Detection and hunting only — do not deploy the framework, do not scan
for exposed consoles, and do not attempt to reproduce any attack.

## 1. Am I even in scope?
- [ ] ARTEX is an agentic attack framework, not a vulnerability: Go
      planner and worker agents with a web console. AntiFox is the same
      code renamed. There is **no CVE** for the framework itself, so
      there is no CISA KEV entry — and none is expected. Do not wait for
      one.
- [ ] Who uses it: reported in intrusions since August 2026 by Storm-0940,
      Storm-3358, VAPOR PANDA and financially motivated operators,
      against Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Okta, AWS, Azure, web
      applications and Active Directory.
- [ ] What you are hunting is **traffic from the framework's agents**,
      not the framework installed on your hosts: branded user agents,
      a framework API key header, unsigned-JWT probes, and connections
      to the AntiFox recording proxy port.
- [ ] An exposed console is not proof of an attack. Researchers, students
      and security teams run these tools, and some hosts are decoys. A
      console address on the internet is a record of exposure, not a
      detection feed — do not block from it without your own evidence.

## 2. The signals (detection)
- [ ] Branded user agent (ARTEX_UA): a request carrying a user agent
      starting `artex-` (for example `artex-pentest/1.0`, or the
      per-role form `artex-<role>/1.0`), `antifox-` (AntiFox), `norma/0.4`,
      or `spa-api-recon`. A careful operator can change these, so a
      missing user agent does not clear a host — it only removes one
      marker.
- [ ] Framework API key header (ARTEX_KEY_HEADER): a request carrying an
      `X-ARTX-KEY` header. Legitimate traffic to your applications does
      not send this header.
- [ ] Unsigned-JWT probe (UNSIGNED_JWT_PROBE): a URI carrying an unsigned
      JWT marker — a base64 `{"alg":"none"}` header (`eyJhbGciOiJub25l`)
      or an `alg` / `none` pair in the query string. Normal JWTs are
      signed; an `alg: none` token is a probe, not a credential.
- [ ] AntiFox recording proxy port (CONSOLE_PORT): a connection to
      destination port **8788**, the AntiFox unauthenticated recording
      proxy. On its own this is weak — port 8788 is not reserved — so it
      only ever counts as a supporting marker, never as an incident by
      itself.
- [ ] Log source: a proxy or WAF log that records the user agent, the
      request headers (or at least header presence), the full URI, and
      the destination port. A stock access log that drops headers cannot
      see markers 2 and 3 — stand up header logging first.

## 3. Correlate
- [ ] Same source address, within 60 minutes: ARTEX_UA plus any other
      signal kind → incident
- [ ] Any single signal kind alone → suspicious; triage it. A lone
      branded user agent can be a researcher running the tool; a lone
      unsigned-JWT probe can be a scanner trying its luck. Check what
      else that source did in the window.
- [ ] CONSOLE_PORT alone → suspicious at most, and only if the source
      also shows other framework markers nearby in time. Never an
      incident on its own.
- [ ] No §2 signals → close with the log-coverage evidence from §2
      (which markers your logs can actually see)

## 4. Triage decision tree
- [ ] Branded user agent + key header or JWT probe → incident: isolate
      the targeted asset, preserve proxy logs, review what the source
      accessed (M365 / Okta / AWS / Azure sign-ins from that source are
      the follow-on to check first).
- [ ] Branded user agent alone → suspicious: check the source against
      your other telemetry (sign-in logs, WAF, EDR) before deciding.
- [ ] Anything confirmed → treat as a host-level intrusion until cleared:
      the framework's agents run real attack tools and keep going until
      they reach a goal.

## Correlation
- [ ] ARTEX_UA + ARTEX_KEY_HEADER / UNSIGNED_JWT_PROBE / CONSOLE_PORT
      on one source within 60 min → incident
- [ ] Any single signal kind alone → suspicious; triage as in §3
- [ ] No §2 signals → close with the log-coverage evidence from §2

## Practice on the synthetic sample
From the repo root:

```bash
python3 07-kev-hunting/detect/artex-agentic-detect.py \
  07-kev-hunting/samples/artex-proxy.log
```

Expect one `[INCIDENT]` (203.0.113.60: branded user agent + key header +
unsigned-JWT probe + recording-proxy port, inside three minutes) and two
`[SUSPICIOUS]` (198.51.100.30: lone branded user agent; 192.0.2.90: lone
unsigned-JWT probe). 192.0.2.10 is clean: normal browser traffic, normal
API calls, no framework markers. All lines are synthetic training data;
the user agents and header names are published detection markers, not
working attack traffic.

Not confirmed, so not used as indicators: the upstream 572-indicator CSV
was not imported — this pack uses only the four named markers above, so
no address, domain, hash or URL from that feed appears here; any other
framework in that collection (Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, and the rest) —
out of scope for this pack, which covers ARTEX and AntiFox only.
